question: According to current criteria, which blood pressure reading defines severe-range hypertension in pregnancy?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These thresholds define hypertension in pregnancy, not severe-range hypertension.
Correct. Severe-range hypertension is defined as systolic ≥160 or diastolic ≥110 mmHg on two readings; it mandates urgent antihypertensive treatment.
This range is neither the standard hypertension threshold nor the severe-range threshold used in practice.
This is above the recognised severe threshold; treatment must be initiated before BP reaches this level.

overallFeedback.feedback: Severe-range hypertension in pregnancy is systolic ≥160 or diastolic ≥110 mmHg. Review the classification in this section.
Well done. Severe-range BP (≥160/110) demands prompt treatment to reduce the risk of stroke and eclampsia.
